post_text:
@Cheval Blanc Courchevel will open two private chalets in December, which can be joined into a single 2,400-square-metre retreat.

The five-bedroom chalet covers 900 square metres. The nine-bedroom one spans 1,500 square metres, with a double-height pool, a dining room and a private wine cellar. Both face the original Maison in the Jardin Alpin of Courchevel 1850, with direct access to the slopes.

Peter Marino designed the common spaces and the Brazilian artist Vik Muniz painted the frescoes. Fifteen butlers and a private culinary team will look after guests, a few steps from Le 1947, the Maison's table led by @Yannick Alléno.

The chalets open under @Mathieu Hellec, General Manager of Cheval Blanc Courchevel since October 2024. It is also the first winter for @Vincent Billiard, named Chief Operating Officer of Cheval Blanc on 5 October, in the leadership team of @Olivier Lefebvre, Chairman and CEO of Cheval Blanc.

The signal: in the Alps, the most exclusive product is no longer a suite but a private house with palace service. @LVMH Hotel Management is building art-filled homes around its Maisons.

Would your guests choose a chalet over the best suite in the house?
